q: 72. French curve are used to draw
explain: A French curve is a template with varying curvature used to draw smooth irregular curves that a compass cannot produce.

q: 73. The size of title block of all size drawing sheet is
explain: As per standard drafting practice, the title block occupies a fixed area of 185 mm × 65 mm regardless of sheet size.

q: 74. The artificial light on the drawing board should be diffused light from the
explain: Light from the left avoids the drafter's hand casting a shadow over the area being drawn.

q: 75. Art of writing title, notes etc. on a drawing is called
explain: Lettering is the drafting skill of neatly writing titles, notes and dimensions on a drawing.

q: 76. Dimension lines and projection line in the drawing are shown by
explain: As per drawing conventions, dimension and projection (extension) lines are drawn as continuous thin lines.

q: 77. System of placing dimension on a drawing work is
explain: Dimensions may be placed using either the aligned method or the unidirectional method, so both systems are valid.

q: 78. When a drawing is made to the same size of the object, the name of the scale is
explain: A scale of 1:1, where drawing size equals actual size, is called full size scale.

q: 79. To draw small objects, the scale used is
explain: Very small objects are drawn larger than actual size using an enlarged (enlarging) scale for clarity.

q: 80. The ratio of distance on the drawing sheet and corresponding actual distance of the object is known as
explain: This ratio, drawing distance to actual distance, is by definition called the Representative Factor (RF).

q: 81. In isometric projection, the receding lines are drawn with the horizontal at
explain: The two receding (isometric) axes are drawn at 30° to the horizontal, with the third axis vertical.

q: 82. In orthographic projection, the line of sight and the plane of projection are
explain: By definition, orthographic projection uses parallel projectors that strike the projection plane perpendicularly.

q: 83. In first angle projection, the object comes
explain: In first angle projection the object is placed in the first quadrant, between the observer and the plane of projection.

q: 84. In third angle projection, if the auxiliary vertical plane is placed to the right of the object, the view obtained is called
explain: In third angle projection the view is projected onto the plane on the same side it is taken from, so a plane to the right of the object gives the right side view.

q: 85. The purpose of sectional view is to show the
explain: A sectional view is created by an imaginary cutting plane specifically to reveal internal (hidden) details of an object.

q: 86. In full sectional view, the object is imagined to be cut off
explain: A full section passes a single cutting plane through the entire object, effectively removing one half of it in the view.

q: 87. The ratio of isometric length and true length of the object is
explain: The isometric scale factor 0.815 can be expressed as the ratio √2:√3, relating isometric length to true length.

q: 88. A circle in isometric projection appears as
explain: Because isometric axes are inclined to the viewing direction, a true circle is foreshortened and appears as an ellipse.

q: 89. In isometric projection, dimension lines are drawn
explain: To remain consistent with the pictorial form, isometric dimension lines are drawn parallel to the isometric axes.

q: 90. Isometric projection of a sphere is a circle having a diameter
explain: Because a sphere looks the same from every direction, its isometric projection is a true circle equal to the sphere's actual diameter.

q: 91. The angle between isometric axes is
explain: The three isometric axes are drawn 120° apart from each other.

q: 92. In isometric projection, circles are represented as ellipse on
explain: Since all three isometric faces are inclined to the line of sight, circles on any face appear as ellipses.

q: 93. The drawing prepared by a pencil without use of drawing instrument is called
explain: A drawing made only with a pencil, without instruments like a scale, compass or set square, is called a freehand sketch.

q: 94. Free hand sketches are used for expressing and recording
explain: Freehand sketches are quick and informal, best suited for capturing initial concepts and new ideas.

q: 95. In sketching, horizontal lines are drawn from
explain: For a right-handed person, drawing horizontal lines left to right gives better control and visibility.

q: 96. Size of letter means the …… of the letter.
explain: Letter 'size' in drafting standards refers to the height of the capital letters.

q: 97. The point in space where parallel lines meet is called
explain: In perspective drawing, parallel lines receding into the distance appear to converge at a vanishing point.

q: 98. The perspective of a circle, when its plane is parallel to other picture plane, is
explain: When a circle's plane is parallel to the picture plane, it is viewed without foreshortening and its perspective remains a circle.

q: 99. When the picture plane coincides with the object, the perspective of the object will be of its
explain: If the picture plane passes through the object itself, there is no projection scaling, so the perspective is the same size as the object.

q: 100. The measurement of standard A2 size drawing sheet in mm is
explain: As per the ISO A-series, the A2 sheet size is 420 mm × 594 mm.

q: 101. The dimension system is unidirectional if
options: dimension in the drawing sheet be read from bottom edge of the drawing sheet
dimension in the drawing sheet be read from bottom and right hand edge of the drawing sheet
dimension in the drawing sheet be read from anywhere of the drawing sheet
explain: In the unidirectional dimensioning system all figures are written horizontally so the whole drawing can be read from the bottom edge of the sheet only.

q: 102. The latter 'H' labeled in a Drawing Pencil indicates
explain: The 'H' grading on a pencil denotes the relative hardness of its lead.

q: 103. The technique for freehand sketch to drawing straight line is
explain: Marking the start and end points first, then joining them, produces a straighter freehand line.

q: 104. Sketching is usually done
explain: Sketching, by definition, is done freehand without the aid of drafting instruments.

q: 105. The ratio of the length on the drawing to the actual length know as
explain: This ratio is formally termed the Representative Factor (RF) of the drawing.

q: 106. The plane on which perspective is formed is called
explain: The perspective image of an object is projected onto the vertical picture plane.

q: 107. In Engineering Drawing, French curves mean
options: drafting tools used to draw non-linear drawings
drafting tools used to draw oblong figures
explain: French curves are drafting templates of varying curvature used to draw smooth non-linear (irregular curved) lines.

q: 108. The set of technical drawings used during the manufacturing phase of product including civil construction are known as:
explain: Detailed drawings used to actually carry out manufacturing or construction work are called working drawings.

q: 109. Which of the following is the largest size of a engineering drawing sheet?
explain: In the ISO A-series, the sheet number decreases as size increases; A0 (841×1189 mm) is the largest of the options listed.

q: 110. The view actually appears to the observer when viewed from a fixed position is called:
explain: A perspective view replicates how an object actually appears to the eye from a fixed viewing point, including apparent size reduction with distance.

q: 111. An isometric projection is pictorial drawing of
explain: Isometric projection is a pictorial representation that shows three faces (views) of an object in a single drawing.

q: 112. Representative fraction when making a drawing in scale of 1 cm =10m will be:
explain: 1 cm = 10 m = 1000 cm, so the RF is 1:1000.

q: 113. Axonometric projection is
explain: Axonometric projection is a category of orthographic (parallel) projection where the object is rotated to show multiple faces.

q: 114. The ratio of the length of the drawing to the actual length of the object is called:
explain: This drawing-to-actual length ratio is termed the representative fraction.

q: 115. Title block gives the information about:
explain: The title block consolidates all key drawing information: title, scale, serial/sheet number, and more.

q: 116. In standard A series drawing sheet, the ratio of length of shorter side to longer side is equal to:
explain: The A-series sheets maintain a constant aspect ratio of shorter side to longer side equal to 1:√2.

q: 117. The plane on which perspective is formed is called
explain: The perspective image is formed on the vertical picture plane positioned between the eye and the object.

q: 118. Drawing made to one half of the actual size is
explain: A scale of 1:2 means the drawing is exactly half the size of the actual object.

q: 119. The set of technical drawings used during the manufacturing phase of a product. including civil construction, are known as:
explain: Drawings that guide the actual manufacturing/construction process are called working drawings.

q: 120. Which of the following is not intended while making a 'sketch' in the context of technical drawings?
options: a quick way to record and idea an idea for work
explain: A sketch is meant as a quick, preliminary freehand record of an idea, not a finished (final) product.

q: 121. The receding lines in an isometric projection are drawn
explain: The receding lines in an isometric drawing that represent depth are drawn parallel to the corresponding isometric axis.

q: 122. The maps which are on sufficiently large scale to enable the individual features shown on the map to be identified on the ground by their shape and position are called:
explain: A large-scale site plan shows enough detail that individual features can be identified on the ground by their shape and position.

q: 123. The letter 'H' labeled in a Drawing pencil indicates
explain: The 'H' grade on a pencil lead denotes its relative hardness.

q: 124. What is the standard size (in mm) of A3 size drawing sheet?
explain: As per ISO A-series, A3 measures 297 mm × 420 mm.

q: 125. First angle projection method and third angle projection method are used in:
explain: First-angle and third-angle projection are the two conventions used specifically for multi-view orthographic drawing.

q: 126. The 'title block' is provided in a drawing sheet at:
explain: By drafting convention the title block is placed in the bottom-right hand corner of the sheet for easy reference when folded.

q: 127. In engineering drawing auxiliary views are used to show details of:
explain: Auxiliary views are projected onto planes parallel to inclined surfaces so their true shape and size can be shown without distortion.

q: 128. Clinograph is a type of:
explain: A clinograph is an adjustable set square whose angle can be varied for drawing lines at any required inclination.

q: 129. Orthographic projection means:
explain: Orthographic projection uses projectors perpendicular to the projection plane, forming right angles, consistent with a right-angled triangle relationship.

q: 130. One of the characteristic features of a perspective drawing is that objects are drawn:
options: larger as their distance from the observer increases
smaller as their distance from the observer increases
explain: Perspective drawing mimics natural vision, where objects appear progressively smaller as their distance from the observer increases.

q: 131. Which of the following theories of mathematics is used by a CAD (Computer Aided Design) software in creating a perspective design?
explain: CAD software uses vector analysis to transform and project 3D object coordinates into a 2D perspective view.

q: 132. "Perspective Drawing" is an approximate representation on a flat surface of an image .......
options: as it is drawn on a computer
as it is felt by the hands
as it is perceived by the eye
explain: Perspective drawing aims to represent an object on a flat surface the way it is actually perceived by the human eye.

q: 133. In the first angle projection the object is assumed to be placed in:
explain: First angle projection, by definition, places the object in the first quadrant, between the observer and the projection plane.

q: 134. Scales usually used in civil engineering drawings are
explain: Because civil structures are large, they are almost always drawn to a reduced scale so they fit on standard sheets.

q: 135. Diagonal Scales are used for measurement of
explain: A diagonal scale can measure three successive units (e.g., metres, decimetres, centimetres) using its diagonal subdivisions.

q: 136. The locus of a point is a ......... when it moves in a plane in such a way that its distance from a fixed line is always a constant.
explain: A point that maintains a constant perpendicular distance from a fixed line traces a straight line parallel to it.

q: 137. The ratio of the shortest distance from the focus to the shortest distance from the directrix is called
explain: This constant ratio, distance from focus to distance from directrix, is by definition the eccentricity of a conic section.

q: 138. As built drawing is normally prepared
explain: As-built drawings document the completed, actual construction and so are prepared after construction finishes.

q: 139. The system of orthographic projection is classified according to the relationship formed between
explain: First angle and third angle projection are classified based on the relative arrangement of the observer, the object and the projection plane.

q: 140. As far as possible drawings shall be prepared with the north n the direction of the
explain: Site/location drawings are conventionally oriented with north pointing toward the top of the sheet.

q: 141. In case of orthographic projection the number of view generally used are
explain: The complete orthographic system generally uses six principal views.

q: 142. Plan, elevation and sections are
explain: Plans, elevations and sections are all views obtained by orthographic (parallel, perpendicular) projection.
